title: Read in one measured column
intent: Let a reader finish a passage without tracking back to the start of the line.
when_to_use: the content is continuous prose the reader works through in order
the page's job is comprehension rather than comparison
when_not_to_use: the content is reference material the reader jumps around, where an index and short titled sections win
the content needs a data display beside the text, where the figure must sit in the flow at full width
rules: body text runs between 60 and 80 characters per line at the widest breakpoint
a section support paragraph stays under 25 words, and anything longer becomes body copy with its own title
the reading column keeps one left edge across every section, so the start of the line never moves
no sidebar carries navigation on the reading page; navigation sits above the column or excludes itself from it
trade_off: One column wastes horizontal space on a wide screen and rules out parallel content, so asides and figures must live in the flow and lengthen the reading order.
failure_mode: The column is stretched wide while the type stays small, so lines run past 110 characters and the reader loses the line return.

example.brief: Post mortem document, around 2000 words, read once by an engineering team.
example.ruling: Family single-column-measure capped at 72 characters, every section titled, figures full width with numbered captions, and no support paragraph above 25 words.
